name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Prediction markets price Republican win at 94%
Democrat Josh Smead has raised only ~$72k with no outside support
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but does not change the partisan baseline
model.rationale: This R+19 open seat gives Republicans a large structural edge, and markets price the race at 94% Republican. The Democrat's minimal fundraising and lack of outside spending give no evidence of a competitive campaign, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based baseline.
model.watch: A surge in Democratic outside spending or polling showing the Republican nominee underperforming in this conservative district would be the main signal of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's 6th District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of R+19, and longtime Representative Sam Graves is retiring. Chris Stigall enters as the Republican nominee with a modest but real war chest of about $600,000 raised, while Democrat Josh Smead has raised under $75,000 and holds little cash. A Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 94% chance of winning. With no evidence of Democratic investment or competitive polling, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands despite the open-seat dynamic.
